clue.text: The hour to be seen round about — so tedious

indicators.note: to be seen round tells us the hour word wraps itself around the next pieces

parts.note: the hour of day is the time
re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that hanging around waiting for the hour to come round is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of 'seen round about', but it is the Latin-derived RE, and 'so' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearying and dull is tiresome; the words are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Tall buildings have some pull

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as TOW-ERS: people who tow certainly exert some pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall structures such as church steeples are towers; people who tow vehicles or barges are those who pull, read as tow-ers.

clue.text: Gunmen take five — that's most unusual

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
to take five is to have a short break, a rest

explanation.surface: Armed men pausing for a breather is a very odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a standard crossword stand-in for gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common or most exceptional.

clue.text: Call for silence, then treat bad break

parts.note: sh is the hushing sound used to ask for quiet

indicators.note: bad says the letters of treat come out wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A doctor hushes the patient before dealing with a nasty fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treat' reads as a verb for medical care, but it is anagram fodder; 'break' as a verb defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces, a direct synonym when break is a verb.

clue.text: For a Greek character to go to church means a lot

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person attending church is described as hugely significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Much and a lot are interchangeable quantity words, as in thanks very much.

clue.text: Sound fellow — though quite a spouter!

indicators.note: Sound at the start tells us to take a word as it is pronounced

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A healthy chap turns out to be a real windbag.
explanation.walkthrough: GEEZER is everyday British slang for a man. 'Sound' looks like an adjective (a sound fellow is a reliable one) but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring that shoots water into the air is a natural spouter, so the definition is a playful description.

clue.text: The individual raising a point with the minister

parts.note: E, east, is one of the compass points
a rector is a parish priest or minister

explanation.surface: A churchgoer stands up to make a point to the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' means a compass point here, not a remark; E is east.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raises or puts up a structure is an erector, the agent noun of erect.

clue.text: Awfully mean rep's reserves

indicators.note: Awfully suggests the letters that follow are in a terrible jumble

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here, giving REPS

explanation.surface: A salesman's backups are described as dreadfully stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges MEANREPS. The two-word answer means substitutes held back in sport, a sense common in British football and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare men are extra players kept back, so they are reserves in the team-sheet sense.

clue.text: Rendering an account

parts.note: reads like settling a bill, but means telling a story or narrating events

explanation.surface: An accountant is presenting the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account' suggests money, but here it is a narrative being told.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate events is to tell or narrate them, so giving a story is this activity.

clue.text: Vigorous preparation for militant action

parts.note: describes an energetic ritual dance performed by warriors before battle

explanation.surface: Activists are getting ready, energetically, for a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Some peoples performed a ceremonial dance to stir warriors before fighting, a literal energetic preparation for combat.

clue.text: Turn out everything after February's turned

indicators.note: after places the word for everything behind the month piece
turned tells us the abbreviation for the month is written back to front

parts.note: Feb is the short form of February
all means everything

explanation.surface: Once February comes round, everything changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' reads as an instruction, but it is the definition, meaning to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To befall is to happen or come to pass, just as things turn out a certain way.

clue.text: Photograph sporting couples

indicators.note: sporting here means wearing or showing off, hinting at the letters dressed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A snapshot of pairs at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as athletic, but it rearranges COUPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a picture taken at very short range, a kind of photo.

clue.text: Trees one maybe put in a different position

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gardener considers moving trees, perhaps one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges TREES plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To resite something is to locate it again somewhere new, a relocation.

clue.text: The home check-up can be most boring

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a home
a test is an examination or check-up

explanation.surface: A home inspection is the dullest job going.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull and lifeless, so the superlative means the dullest.

clue.text: He sets all straight — it's not left to the queen

parts.note: the opposite of left is right
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the queen

explanation.surface: A fixer insists that he, not the monarch, settles things.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a crossword convention for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rights wrongs puts matters straight, the agent noun of right as a verb.

clue.text: A capital operator!

parts.note: capital hints at the head, so this is a surgeon who operates on the brain rather than a financier

explanation.surface: A praise for a smooth City financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money or excellence; its root sense is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon working inside the skull operates on the head, which capital originally meant.

clue.text: Anything but agreeable parties

parts.note: reads like dull social gatherings, but means quarrelling splinter groups

explanation.surface: Some social gatherings are thoroughly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' suggests celebrations; here they are political or group sides that disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissenting groups within a body are disagreeing sides, so they are hardly in agreement.

clue.text: Cheat, worn-out and guilt-ridden

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
trite means hackneyed or worn-out

explanation.surface: A swindler, exhausted, is full of remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow for wrongdoing makes one penitent and remorseful.

clue.text: Premeditated the routing of that rough foe

indicators.note: routing means scattering in defeat, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A planned attack routs a brutal enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: As held, 'the rough foe' gives only 11 letters with a spare E; 'routing of' must rearrange THAT ROUGH FOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned in advance is the sense, as in the legal phrase malice planned beforehand.

clue.text: Balancing — in time

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: the verb form of even, and the period after afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening scales or accounts means balancing them; the late part of the day is a time.

clue.text: Some watch a bit at home

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A naturalist spends some time observing animals at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's natural environment is where it lives, its home.

clue.text: There's panic about the cold when exceptional

indicators.note: about says the panic word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: People panic about the cold only when it is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means rarely found, so in short supply and out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Value of the female donkey?

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
-ess is the suffix marking a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders what a jenny donkey is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding the feminine suffix -ESS to ASS gives a mock word for a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to estimate the worth of something, to value it as a verb.

clue.text: Apparently found something amusing in rows about certain races

indicators.note: about tells us the rows word goes around the races

parts.note: tiered means arranged in rows or layers
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Spectators in tiered seats laughed at the race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: TT races are the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races. 'Apparently' fits because a giggle only shows amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggling nervously is laughing, which shows that a person found something funny.

clue.text: A graduate copper's counting on this

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the possessive s is kept

explanation.surface: A graduate police officer is relied upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires is a device people use to count.

clue.text: Bold man giving a girl a ring

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a girl
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A brave suitor proposes to a girl with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A courageous man admired for his deeds is the classic brave champion.

clue.text: Very large bloom once highly esteemed by Egyptians

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large in clothing sizes
an iris is a flower, a bloom

explanation.surface: A huge flower was prized in ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a British clothing-size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This god of the dead and the afterlife was worshipped in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Secretes damaged antique coin

indicators.note: damaged suggests the word is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone hides away a damaged old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges SECRETES.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silver coin of ancient Rome, worth a quarter of a denarius.

clue.text: Express despair about the French transport in winter

indicators.note: about says the despairing word goes around the French article

parts.note: to sigh is to express despair
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone groans about the French way of getting around in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-mounted vehicle drawn over snow is a means of travel in snowy months.

clue.text: A strong point in favour of long hair

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Long hair has one great advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong point' sounds like an advantage but means a fortified place.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold is a defensive position, a military strong point.
